questions.q_en:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Vaccination also plays a crucial role in protecting vulnerable populations, including infants, the elderly, and immunocompromised individuals, by contributing to herd immunity.

B. Similarly, vaccines against bacterial infections like diphtheria, tetanus, and pertussis have saved countless lives and prevented severe disabilities.

C. For example, the widespread use of the measles vaccine has prevented millions of deaths and complications like blindness and encephalitis.

D. Routine immunization programs have dramatically decreased the incidence of many infectious diseases, such as measles, mumps, and rubella.
questions.solution_en:

Sentence C provides a specific example of the measles vaccine's effectiveness in preventing deaths and complications. So, 'D' and 'C' together form a pair. Sentence B continues by emphasizing the lifesaving benefits of vaccines against bacterial infections. Finally, sentence A concludes the paragraph by explaining how vaccination protects vulnerable populations through herd immunity.

Therefore, the right sequence to present a coherent paragraph about the importance and impact of vaccination is DCBA. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

S3: ___________________________

S4 states that those were not rubies but actually a far rarer mineral. Sentence Q does not fit in as it tells about another person, Rossman, whereas sentence S4 talks about someone by the name of 'Pain'.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

The girl told her friends that she had taken her little brother to walk in the garden.
options_en: The girl said to her friends, "I am taking my little brother to walk in the garden."
The girl said to her friends, "I took my little brother to walk in the garden."
The girl said to her friends, "She took the garden to walk in my little brother."
The girl said to her friends, "She has been taken my little brother to walk in the garden."
questions.solution_en:
The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Past Perfect Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Direct Speech will be in Past Simple or Present Perfect tense.

Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 + Object) will be converted into Past Simple (Subject + V2 + Object).

For example:

He said that Arya had sent him a book. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "Arya sent me a book" (Direct Speech)

OR

Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 +Object) will be converted into Present Perfect (Subject + has/have + V3 +Object).

For example:

He said that he had got a new job. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I have got a new job." (Direct Speech)

The first case is applicable here (past simple).

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

· The reporting verb 'told' is changed into 'said to'.

· The pronoun 'she' is changed into 'I'.

· The possessive determiner 'her' is changed into 'my'.

· Verb 'Had taken' is changed into 'took'.

Option (a) is eliminated because it is in present continuous tense. Option (c) is eliminated because the meaning of the sentence has been changed. Option (d) is eliminated because the verb is in passive voice which is contextually incorrect in this case.

Therefore, the correct answer is: The girl said to her friends, "I took my little brother to walk in the garden."

questions.q_en:
Spot the erroneous part if any, in the following sentence.

The plumber/ fixed the leak (A)/ after the water (B)/ had flood (C)/ the basement. / No error (D).
questions.solution_en:
The erroneous part in the sentence is (C). The error in segment (C) relates to the verb tense agreement. The sentence describes two past actions: the flooding of the basement and the plumber fixing the leak. The sequence of events indicates that the flooding occurred before the plumber fixed the leak. To express this sequence of events properly, the past perfect tense is used to indicate an action that occurred before another past action. In this case, "had flooded" (past participle form (V3)) should be used instead of "had flood" (flood is the base form of the verb) to convey that the flooding happened prior to the plumber fixing the leak. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: "The plumber fixed the leak after the water had flooded the basement."

questions.solution_en:
The part given in option (d) has the error. The definite article 'an' can be used for a word that starts with a vowel sound. 'Helicopter' doesn't start with a vowel sound. So, 'an' cannot be used here. it must be replaced with 'a' which is used before words with consonant sounds.

The correct sentence is: The chief guest is to be carried by a helicopter from here.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in past continuous tense.

A) They were playing football every weekend.

B) They have played football every weekend.

C) They played football every weekend.

D) They are playing football every weekend.
questions.solution_en:
The option that expresses the given sentence in past continuous tense is (a). The past continuous tense is used to describe an action that was ongoing or in progress at a specific time in the past. It is formed by using the past tense of the verb "to be" (was/were) and the present participle form (V4) of the main verb (-ing form) (playing). Only sentence A follows the correct structure of past continuous tense. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

Note:

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

questions.q_en:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

P. into long-duration spaceflight, advanced propulsion systems,

Q. the ambitious goal of landing astronauts on Mars

R. and sustainable life support systems

S. within the next decade fuels extensive research
questions.solution_en:
The sentence begins with part Q, "The ambitious goal of landing astronauts on Mars," which introduces the main subject of the sentence - the ambitious goal. This part clearly sets up what the goal is and what it does.

Part S, "within the next decade fuels extensive research," logically follows Q. "within the next decade" specifies the timeframe for the goal mentioned in Q, and "fuels extensive research" is the verb phrase describing the action of the "ambitious goal."

Next, part P, "into long-duration spaceflight, advanced propulsion systems," specifies the areas into which the extensive research (mentioned in S) is directed. The preposition "into" links directly to "research."

Finally, part R, "and sustainable life support systems," completes the list of research areas initiated in P, using the conjunction "and" to add the final element to the series.

Thus, the correct and meaningful order of the sentence is QSPR.

The complete sentence after rearrangement is: The ambitious goal of landing astronauts on Mars within the next decade fuels extensive research into long-duration spaceflight, advanced propulsion systems, and sustainable life support systems.

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

The government's new initiative to provide vocational training / aim to equip young people with practical skills, / thereby enhancing their employability in the competitive job market.

thereby enhancing their employability in the competitive job market
aim to equip young people with practical skills,
questions.solution_en:
The error is in the part "aim to equip young people with practical skills,". The subject of this clause is "The government's new initiative," which is singular. Therefore, the verb should be in its singular form. "Aim" (plural/base form) should be "aims" (singular).

Correct Sentence: The government's new initiative to provide vocational training aims to equip young people with practical skills, thereby enhancing their employability in the competitive job market.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

Note:

· Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. "Initiative" (singular subject) requires the singular verb "aims."

· V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s): 'aims' is the V5 form of the verb 'aim'.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

Raj said to Rajiv, "Don't justify your mistakes."
options_en: Raj advised Rajiv not to justify your mistakes.
Raj advised Rajiv not to justified his mistakes.
Raj advised Rajiv don't justify his mistakes.
Raj advised Rajiv not to justify his mistakes.
questions.solution_en:
Imperative Sentences sometimes begin with Negative Commands like "Don't".

As required, "Said/ Say" is changed into "Asked/ Ask", "Told/ Tell", "Advised/ Advise" etc.

"Not + To+ Verb" is used in these sentences. For example, "don't go" changes into "not to go" in Indirect speech.

In this context, "Don't ......" changes into "not to ......".

For example:

My friend said to me, "Don't go to Kolkata"." (Direct Speech)

My friend advised me not to go to Kolkata. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

Direct SpeechIndirect Speech
said toadvised
Don'tnot to
yourhis

Therefore, the correct answer is: (d) Raj advised Rajiv not to justify his mistakes.

questions.q_en: Select the sentence in which the '-ing' form of verb expresses the continuity of an action/event.
options_en: Writing poetry is a relaxing activity.
I have a career in writing.
The students are discussing the project details.
He bought a writing pad for his notes.
questions.solution_en:
Option (c): The '-ing' form of the verb "discussing" in this sentence is part of the present continuous tense ("are discussing"), which indicates that the action is happening now and expresses the continuity of the event.

Option (a): Here, the '-ing' form "writing" is a gerund, which functions as a noun and does not express the continuity of an action/event while the '-ing' form "relaxing" is an adjective modifying the noun 'activity'.

Option (b): Here also, the '-ing' form "writing" is a gerund, which functions as a noun and does not express the continuity of an action/event.

Option (d): The '-ing' form "writing" here is an adjective describing the type of pad. It does not indicate the continuity of any action/event.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

Note:

Gerund: Gerund is a verb form that functions as a noun, ending in -ing. A gerund can be either the subject or object of a sentence in English. Example: "Everybody enjoyed her dancing and singing at the party." The words 'dancing' and 'singing' are gerunds.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech:

Kanhaiya said to me, "Do you want to sing?"
options_en: Kanhaiya enquires if I want to sing.
Kanhaiya said that whether I would sing.
Kanhaiya said that I would sing or not.
Kanhaiya asked me if I wanted to sing.
questions.solution_en:
In the case of Interrogative sentences like this, "said" in Direct Speech is changed into "enquired (of)", "wanted to know", "asked", etc.

In Indirect speech, the verb is always placed after the subject, unlike in Direct Speech.

If there is a question in the Direct Speech whose answer can come as "Yes" or "No" in the Indirect Speech, we should use the conjunctions "if" or "whether".

For example:

Ravi said to me, "Is she studying?" (Direct Speech)

Ravi asked me if she was studying. (Indirect Speech)

Also, the sentence in the Direct Speech is in the Simple Present tense. So, the tense in the Indirect Speech should be in the Simple Past tense.

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

Said to-Asked/enquired

Do-If

Accordingly, the sentence that follows the above rules of Indirect speech is "Kanhaiya asked me if I wanted to sing."

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

Alan said that he would go to the cinemas to watch the latest movie.
options_en: Alan said, "I go to the cinemas to watch the latest movie."
Alan said, "I will be going to the cinemas to watch the latest movie."
Alan said, "I will go to the cinemas to watch the latest movie."
Alan said, "I would have gone to the cinemas to watch the latest movie."
questions.solution_en:
The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Present Conditional Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Direct Speech will be in Future Simple Tense.

Present Conditional (Subject + would/should + V1 +object) will be converted into Future Simple (Subject + will/shall + V1 + object).

For example:

He said that he would bring Karan home on Sunday. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I will bring Karan home on Sunday." (Direct Speech)

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:
Indirect SpeechDirect Speech
said thatsaid
heI
would gowill go

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

NOTE:

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate collocation to substitute the underlined phrase in the given sentence.

I look forward for seeing you tomorrow at the party.
questions.solution_en:
The phrase "look forward to" is a common collocation used to express anticipation or excitement about something in the future. It is followed by a gerund or a noun phrase. The preposition "to" is used to indicate the direction or goal of the anticipation. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

When certain verbs are followed by specific prepositions, they form collocations that have become idiomatic or conventional in the language. These collocations often have a fixed structure, and using the correct preposition is essential to convey the intended meaning.

The final sentence would be: I look forward to seeing you tomorrow at the party.
